releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.39

### New
- **Party:** party members are now shown on your screen as heads, at the place where they are in the world, like a waypoint (new option "Member heads on screen", on by default). The head is always the same size, whatever the distance, and the distance in meters is written under it (1.2km for long distances). When you aim at a head it grows slightly and the player's name appears above it. Close to the player the head fades out together with the name and distance; the new option "Head fades out closer than" (default 10 blocks, 0 = never) sets how close. Heads of members who are far away need coordinates enabled in the party (the leader starts a vote); members you can see in the world are shown without it.

## Changes since 1.0.37

### New
- **Locator Bar:** new HUD module for the vanilla locator bar (the bar that shows other players and waypoints, Minecraft 1.21.6 and newer). Options:
  - **Player heads:** players on the bar are shown as their head, with an outline in the color of their locator bar waypoint.
  - **Show direction:** shows the compass direction you are facing (N, NE, E, ...) in the middle of the bar.
  - **On the XP bar:** keeps the experience bar and draws the locator icons on top of it.
  - **Show player name:** names above the icons (never, on hover or always).
  - **Show icons:** turn off to get small colored squares instead of icons.
  - **Text shadow:** shadow for the direction and names.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.35

### Fixes
- **Party:** a player who leaves the server and joins again now gets back into the party. Before, the others still listed them but their client had forgotten the party, so nothing worked. After you reconnect, the mod asks your old party members for the party state (only people from your old party are trusted, and only for 30 minutes). If you restarted the game, you still need a new invite.
- **Party:** the party now checks who is on the server. A member who left is shown as offline in the party menu (grey name), you get a chat message when they leave or come back, and they no longer receive messages or block coordinate votes while they are gone.

### Improvements
- **Markers:** new "Beacon" option draws a translucent light beam above every marker, visible through walls. Its thickness can be changed and defaults to 0.6 blocks, the same as a player hitbox.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.34

### Improvements
- **Optimization:** new "Animate Only Visible Textures" option. Animated block textures (magma, sea lanterns, portals and so on) are now sent to the GPU only while a block that uses them is in a visible part of the world, instead of all the time. This helps most with high-resolution texture packs (128x and up). Water, lava, fire and portal textures are always animated. The world rebuilds once when you switch the option on or off, and the option is locked when Sodium is installed, because Sodium already does this.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.33

### Fixes
- **Markers / Party:** a marker you place no longer shows up twice on your own screen. Some servers send your own private message back to you ("You whisper to ..."), and the mod used to treat that echo as a marker from the person you wrote to. Every party message now carries the sender's name, so your own echo is ignored and a marker is always labeled with the player who actually placed it. Older mod versions still work: they ignore the extra field.
- **Markers:** the same target marked twice within a moment (or by the same player again) is now merged into one marker, and player names are compared without regard to capital letters.

### Improvements
- **Party:** new "Party message log (diagnostics)" option writes the raw party messages to the game log, which helps to find out what a particular server sends.

mods.name: AIO PvP
mods.description: All-in-one PvP HUD and visual tweaks in vanilla style.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.32

### Fixes
- **Fight Report:** a fight you won is no longer reported as "undecided" on practice and minigame servers (such as Stray.gg) that remove the killed player at once and send neither a death status nor health. A player disappearing shortly after your last hit now counts as a win, and so does a kill message in chat that names the opponent together with you or a kill word ("slain", "killed", ...). Fights where the opponent just walks away still end as undecided.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.31

### Fixes
- **Markers:** a ping from a party member no longer shows up twice (the same message arriving twice is now counted once, and a repeated marker at the same spot refreshes instead of stacking). Markers also follow the real field of view, so they stay on their target when you zoom with another mod.
- **Waypoints:** the beam now leaves a gap where the icon (and its name) hangs, so it no longer cuts through the picture.
- **Hit Color:** the color is shown only after you (or a mob) are hit by an attacker. Burning, lava, falling and other damage without an attacker no longer turn the whole model red.
- **Cooldown Fix:** it no longer hides your hand while you mine or place blocks. It now resets only the attack cooldown, like the server does, and leaves the hand animation alone.

### Improvements
- **Waypoints:** click a waypoint in the list to edit it (name, coordinates, color, icon), then Save or Cancel.

mods.name: AIO PvP
mods.description: All-in-one PvP HUD and visual tweaks in vanilla style.

releases.notes:
## Changes since 1.0.30

### New modules
- **Waypoints:** save places with a name, color and an optional pixel-art icon. A beam marks each waypoint in the world; the name and distance show when you look at it. Manage them in a dedicated menu (type coordinates, pick a color, draw an icon) or with `/waypoint`. Waypoints are saved per server/world and dimension, and can be created automatically when you die.
- **Markers:** press the middle mouse button to ping a block or a mob. The marker shows the block (or mob) icon, distance and coordinates. A marker on a mob follows it and disappears when it dies or despawns.
- **Party (client-side):** invite players who also use the mod. Roles are Leader, Inviter and Member; the leader can kick players and give the Inviter rank. Party members see each other's markers. Member coordinates are only shown after everyone agrees in a vote (CS2-style popup). It has its own menu with player heads, ranks and settings. No server mod is needed: messages go through private messages (`/msg` by default) and are hidden in the recipient's chat. Different mod versions stay compatible.
- **Sounds:** change the volume of any Minecraft sound by name (0-200%), with search and a hint to enable subtitles to find sound names.
- **Optimization:** Entity Culling, Fog Occlusion and No Error Context. An option is locked, with the reason shown, when another installed mod (e.g. Sodium) already does the same thing.

### Improvements
- HUD labels (FPS, Ping, CPS, Day, Clock, Coordinates, Compass) and the media player: new corner rounding option; brackets `[ ]` for text labels.
- Media Player: the buttons are spaced out and clickable, the player stays on screen in chat, inventory and other windows, and every part (title, artist, buttons, progress bar) has its own color.
- New Blockbench-style color picker (hue bar, hex field, recent colors) in the waypoint menus.
- The party vote popup is a movable HUD element ("Party Vote") in the HUD editor.
- Settings: "Remember risky modules" keeps Freelook and Instant Hit enabled between game launches, after an explicit risk warning.
- The config file now stores a format version for safer future updates.

### Notes
- Party, Markers and Waypoints are client-side only. Server admins can see the private messages the Party module sends in their logs.

releases.notes:
## First release for Minecraft 26.3

The full mod from the 1.21.11 version, ported to Minecraft 26.3. Every module, the menu, HUD editor, Fight Report and settings work the same way.

### Requirements

- Fabric Loader 0.20.1 or newer
- Fabric API 0.166.2+26.3 or newer
- Java 25
- Mod Menu (optional, adds a config button to the mod list)

### Changes since 1.0.29

- Player Health Indicators: new "Max distance" setting (8 to 64 blocks, default 32). Hearts above players farther away aren't drawn, which saves frame time on crowded servers.

### Note for 26.3

Minecraft 26.3 replaced its input system (SDL instead of GLFW), so keyboard key codes changed. If you copy a config from another Minecraft version, set your module keybinds and Command Keys binds again. Mouse binds carry over.

## Changes since 1.0.27

- Fight Report: a kill now counts as a win on servers that don't send other players' health. The mod uses the server's death signal, so these fights no longer end as "Undecided".
- Freelook: the mouse wheel moves the camera closer or farther (1 to 20 blocks) while Freelook is active in third person. The hotbar slot doesn't change.
